extracted.intended_audience: recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards (grant/contract administrators), pass-through entities, institutions of higher education, state/local governments, and Indian Tribes
extracted.subtask_description: Federal cost principles and allowability standards for costs under Federal awards, including indirect cost rates, required certifications, allowable/unallowable items, personnel compensation and fringe benefit rules, and special considerations for states, local governments, tribes, and IHEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time extension of indirect rates
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or subrecipient with a current Federal negotiated indirect cost rate may apply for a one-time extension of that agreement for up to four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension is subject to review and approval by the cognizant agency for indirect costs; if granted, the recipient/subrecipient may not request a rate review until the extension period ends and must re-apply to negotiate a new rate when the extension ends. After a new rate is negotiated, the recipient/subrecipient may again apply for a one-time extension of the new rate under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reports certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial reports must include a certification signed by an official authorized to legally bind the recipient certifying the report is true, complete, and accurate and that expenditures are for purposes of the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must include awareness of criminal, civil or administrative penalties for false information (citing U.S. Code Title 18 §1001 and Title 31 §§3729-3730 and 3801-3812).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient certification to pass-through entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Subrecipients must certify to the pass-through entity whenever applying for funds, requesting payment, and submitting financial reports with prescribed certification language regarding truthfulness and potential consequences for false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each certification must be maintained pursuant to §200.334 and applies to all tiers of subrecipients; certification wording and cited statutes are specified in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification for cost allocation plan or indirect cost rate proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Each cost allocation plan or indirect cost rate proposal must be certified by the recipient using the Certificate of Cost Allocation Plan or Certificate of Indirect Costs as set forth in appendices III–VII and IX of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate must be signed on behalf of the recipient by an individual at a level no lower than the vice president or chief financial officer. Failure to submit a certified proposal may result in disallowance or unilateral establishment of an indirect cost rate by the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to submit certified indirect cost proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Government may either disallow all indirect costs or unilaterally establish an indirect cost rate when the recipient fails to submit a certified proposal for establishing a rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any unilateral rate should be based upon audited historical data or other furnished data demonstrating exclusion of unallowable costs, must ensure potentially unallowable costs are not reimbursed, and the recipient may instead use the de minimis indirect cost rate (§200.414(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit 'major nonprofit organization' certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit organizations must certify that they did not meet the definition of a major nonprofit organization as defined in §200.414(a), if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required certification in the indirect cost proposal process where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of lobbying requirements for indirect cost proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must certify that the requirements and standards for lobbying (see §200.450) have been met when submitting its indirect cost rate proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is a required element of the indirect cost proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central service cost allocation plan for states/local governments/tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: A central service cost allocation plan is established to allow departments within a State, local government, or Indian Tribe to claim a portion of centralized service costs incurred in proportion to the award's activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized service costs include examples such as motor pools, computer centers, purchasing, and accounting; the plan creates a reasonable and consistent process to identify and assign central service costs to benefitted activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate indirect cost rate per operating department
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual operating departments typically need a separate indirect cost rate proposal to claim indirect costs under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs include indirect costs originating in the operating department and costs of central governmental services distributed through the central service cost allocation plan that are not treated as direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency service costing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an operating department provides services to another department of the same State/local government/Tribe, the cost of services may include allowable direct costs plus a pro-rated share of indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard indirect cost rate equal to 15 percent of the direct salaries and wages for providing the service (excluding overtime, shift premiums, and fringe benefits) may be used instead of determining actual indirect costs. These services do not include centralized services included in central service cost allocation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs incurred by states/local governments on behalf of IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred or paid by a State or local government on behalf of and in direct benefit to its IHEs are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such costs (e.g., fringe benefit programs like pension and FICA) are allowable provided they: meet the requirements of §§200.402–200.411; are properly supported by approved cost allocation plans per applicable cost accounting principles; and are not otherwise borne directly or indirectly by the Federal Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAS compliance for large IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: An IHE that receives an aggregate total of $50 million or more in Federal awards and instruments subject to this subpart in its most recently completed fiscal year must comply with the Cost Accounting Standards Board's standards at 48 CFR 9905.501, .502, .505, and .506.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAS-covered contracts and subcontracts awarded to IHEs are subject to the broader CAS requirements at 48 CFR 9900–9999 and 48 CFR part 30 (FAR Part 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for selected items of cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles provided in this section apply to establishing the allowability of certain items of cost, in addition to other requirements of this subpart, whether or not a cost is treated as direct or indirect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is not comprehensive; failure to mention an item does not imply allowability or unallowability. Determinations should be based on treatment of similar items and principles in §§200.402–200.411; where there's a discrepancy between a specific Federal award and these provisions, the Federal award governs. Criteria in §200.403 must be applied in determining allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable advertising costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The only allowable advertising costs are those solely for: (1) recruitment of personnel required for performance of a Federal award; (2) procurement of goods and services for the Federal award; (3) disposal of scrap or surplus materials acquired in performance of the award (except when reimbursed at predetermined amount); and (4) program outreach and other specific purposes necessary to meet Federal award requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising media includes magazines, newspapers, radio/TV, direct mail, exhibits, and electronic transmittals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable public relations costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The only allowable public relations costs are: (1) costs specifically required by the Federal award; (2) costs of communicating with the public and press about specific activities or accomplishments resulting from the award; and (3) costs of conducting general liaison with news media and government public relations officers limited to communication necessary to keep the public informed on matters of public concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public relations is defined as activities dedicated to maintaining or promoting favorable relations with the community or public at large or segments thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable advertising and public relations costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Unallowable costs include all advertising/public relations costs other than those specified as allowable, costs of meetings/conventions/events related to other activities of the entity (including displays, meeting rooms, hospitality suites, salaries for exhibit/set-up staff), promotional items and memorabilia, and advertising/public relations designed solely to promote the recipient or subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also see §200.432 regarding meetings and conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory council costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by internal or external advisory councils or committees are allowable if authorized by statute, the Federal agency, or as an indirect cost where allocable to Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.444 which applies to States, local governments, and Indian Tribes for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcoholic beverages
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of alcoholic beverages is unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni activities (IHEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by IHEs for, or in support of, alumni activities are unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit services — allowability and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonably proportionate share of the costs of audits required by and performed in accordance with the Single Audit Act Amendments of 1996 and the requirements of this part are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unallowable audit costs include any costs when audits required by the Single Audit Act and subpart F were not conducted or not in accordance with requirements, and (except as provided) costs of auditing a non-Federal entity exempted from audit due to expenditures under Federal awards being less than $1,000,000 during its fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement audits and agreed-upon procedures (pass-through entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs of a financial statement audit of a recipient or subrecipient that does not currently have a Federal award may be included in the indirect cost pool for a cost allocation plan or indirect cost proposal. Pass-through entities may charge Federal awards for the cost of agreed-upon procedures engagements to monitor subrecipients exempt from Single Audit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such agreed-upon procedures engagements are allowable only if: (1) conducted in accordance with GAGAS or applicable international attestation standards; (2) paid for and arranged by the pass-through entity; and (3) limited in scope to specified compliance requirements (allowed/unallowed activities, allowable costs/cost principles, eligibility, reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad debts (debts determined to be uncollectable), including losses from uncollectable accounts and other claims, are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related collection and legal costs arising from such debts are also unallowable. See §200.428 for related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonding costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonding costs arise when assurance against financial loss is required (e.g., bid, performance, payment, advance payment, infringement, fidelity bonds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of bonding required under the Federal award's terms and conditions are allowable. Costs of bonding required by the recipient/subrecipient in general operations are allowable as an indirect cost to the extent they are in accordance with sound business practice and rates/premiums are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections of improper payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred by a recipient or subrecipient to recover improper payments, including overpayments, are allowable as either direct or indirect costs, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts collected may be used in accordance with cash management standards described in §200.305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencements and convocations (IHEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred for commencements and convocations are unallowable for IHEs, except as activity costs provided for in Appendix III, (B)(9) Student Administration and Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation—personal services: general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation for personal services includes all remuneration for services of employees rendered during the period of performance and is allowable to the extent it satisfies the specific requirements of this part and that total compensation for individuals is reasonable, conforms to written policy consistently applied, follows an appointment in accordance with laws/policies, and is determined and supported as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation may include wages, salaries, and certain fringe benefits addressed in §200.431.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation—reasonableness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation for employees engaged in work on Federal awards will be reasonable to the extent consistent with that paid for similar work in other activities of the recipient/subrecipient or comparable to labor market rates where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where required kinds of employees are not found in other activities of the recipient, comparison should be to similar work in the labor market in which the recipient competes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional activities outside the recipient/subrecipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless expressly authorized by the Federal agency, recipients must follow written policies concerning permissible extent of professional services provided outside the recipient for extra outside pay; absent adequate policies the Federal Government may require allocation of professional staff effort between recipient activities and non-organizational professional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate arrangements governing compensation must be negotiated case-by-case if agency considers outside effort excessive or inconsistent with conflicts-of-interest terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compensation ceilings and unallowable compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs unallowable under other sections remain unallowable under compensation provisions; allowable compensation for certain employees may be subject to statutory ceilings (e.g., 10 U.S.C. 3744(a)(16), 41 U.S.C. 1127, 41 U.S.C. 4304(a)(16)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other types of Federal awards may have other statutory ceilings; check relevant statutes for covered compensation, employees, and ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for compensation policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Special consideration in allowability will be given to changes in a recipient's compensation policy resulting in substantial increases in employees' compensation, particularly when concurrent with increased Federal award ratio, or changes due to Federal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentive compensation based on cost reduction, efficient performance, suggestion awards, or safety awards is allowable to the extent that overall compensation is reasonable and such costs are paid/accrued according to an agreement entered in good faith before services rendered or according to an established plan consistently followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for documentation of personnel expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to Federal awards for salaries and wages must be based on records that accurately reflect work performed and be supported by a system of internal control ensuring charges are accurate, allowable, and properly allocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be official, reasonably reflect total activity not exceeding 100% of compensated activities (IBS for IHEs), encompass federally-assisted and other activities on an integrated basis (subsidiary records allowed), comply with recipient accounting policies, and support distribution of salary/wages among cost objectives where employees work on multiple activities. Budget estimates alone do not qualify except for interim use under specified conditions (system produces reasonable approximations; significant changes promptly entered; periodic after-the-fact reviews and adjustments). Records may express activity categories as percentage distributions; precise assessment not required for IHEs. Records meeting these standards generally preclude additional support except where referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timekeeping for nonexempt employees
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to documentation meeting paragraph (g)(1) standards, charges for salaries and wages of nonexempt employees must be supported by records indicating total number of hours worked each day in accordance with DOL FLSA regulations (29 CFR part 516).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries and wages of employees used to meet cost sharing requirements must be supported in the same manner as salaries and wages claimed for reimbursement from Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute systems for states/local governments/tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: States, local governments, and Indian Tribes may use substitute processes or systems (e.g., random moment sampling, rolling time studies, case counts) for allocating salaries and wages to Federal awards if approved by the cognizant agency for indirect cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such systems may be used in place of or in addition to standard personnel records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical sampling standards for substitute systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute systems that use sampling methods must meet acceptable statistical sampling standards, including: sampling universe includes all employees whose salaries are allocated based on sample results; sample covers the entire period; results are statistically valid and applied to the period sampled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocating charges for supervisors and clerical/support staff based on sampled employees is acceptable. Less than full compliance may be accepted by the cognizant agency if allocations to Federal awards will be minimal or the proposed system results in lower costs to Federal awards than a fully compliant system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of alternative performance/outcome-based proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognizant agencies for indirect costs are encouraged to approve alternative proposals based on outcomes and milestones for program performance when clearly documented as an alternative to standard personnel record requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such plans are acceptable only when approved by the cognizant agency for indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blended funding and performance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For Federal awards of similar purpose or approved blended funding, recipients may submit performance plans that incorporate funds from multiple Federal awards and account for combined use based on performance-oriented metrics if approved in advance by all involved Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must request waiver of personnel record requirements based on documentation describing charging methods, relating charging to specific activity applicable to all fund sources, and based on quantifiable measures of activity in relation to time charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal authority to require personnel activity reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient's records do not meet the standards described, the Federal Government may require personnel activity reports, including prescribed certifications, or equivalent documentation supporting the records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organizations — compensation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For compensation to members of nonprofit organizations (trustees, directors, associates, officers, or immediate families), a determination must be made that compensation is reasonable for actual personal services rendered rather than a distribution of earnings above actual costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation may include directors' fees, incentive awards, off-site/incentive pay, location allowances, hardship pay, and cost-of-living differentials; determination focuses on reasonableness for services rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE-specific personnel compensation rules — allowable activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to Federal awards may include reasonable amounts for activities contributing and directly related to work under an agreement (e.g., special lectures, writing reports/articles, developing protocols, managing project-specific data, coordinating research subjects, attending meetings/conferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incidental activities authorized under institutional policy (at a rate not to exceed IBS) do not need to be included in detailed personnel records but must be either in the award budget or approved in writing by the Federal agency to be charged directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Base Salary (IBS) and salary basis for faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for work performed on Federal awards by faculty during the academic year are allowable at the IBS rate; charges may not exceed the proportionate share of the IBS for the period worked on the award unless prior agency approval is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IBS is annual compensation paid by an IHE for an individual's appointment and excludes income earned outside duties for the IHE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-IHE consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: Intra-IHE consulting by faculty should generally be undertaken as an IHE responsibility requiring no compensation in addition to IBS; in unusual cross-department or separate/remote operations where work is additional to regular responsibilities, additional compensation above IBS is allowable if expressly authorized in the award or approved in writing by the Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra service pay (overload) for IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra service pay representing overload compensation is allowable if conditions are met: (i) IHE has consistent written policies applied uniformly; (ii) consistent written definition of work covered by IBS; (iii) supplementation commensurate with IBS pay rate and additional work; (iv) salaries fall within documented salary structure; and (v) total salaries charged to Federal awards are subject to documentation standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra service pay tied to intra-IHE consulting is subject to same requirements as other extra service pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods outside the academic year (IHEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for work performed by faculty on Federal awards during periods not included in the base salary period must be at a rate not more than the IBS, except where teaching activity during those periods must be based on the IHE's written policy governing compensation for teaching assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time faculty salary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for work performed on Federal awards by part-time faculty must be determined at a rate not more than that regularly paid for part-time assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbatical leave costs rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of leaves of absence for graduate work or sabbatical study, travel, or research are allowable provided the IHE has a uniform written sabbatical policy for instruction and research personnel and costs are equitably allocated among related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where sabbatical leave is included in fringe benefits assessed as a direct charge, the aggregate amount must be reasonable in relation to the IHE's actual experience; allocation and timing rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary rates for non-faculty regarding extra service pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-faculty full-time professional personnel may earn extra service pay in accordance with the IHE's written policy and the section governing extra service pay for faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits (allowances and services in addition to salaries) such as leave, insurance, pensions, and unemployment benefits are allowable provided they are reasonable and required by law, employee agreement, or established policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fringe benefits must be allocated to Federal awards and other activities consistent with the pattern of benefits attributable to the individuals or groups and charged as direct or indirect costs following accounting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave fringe benefits — criteria and accounting basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of leave (paid during authorized absences) is allowable if: (1) provided under established written leave policies; (2) equitably allocated to all related activities including Federal awards; and (3) the accounting basis (cash or accrual) selected for costing each type of leave is consistently followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under cash basis, leave cost recognized when taken/paid; payments for unused leave at termination allowable in year of payment and allocated as general admin expense or included in fringe rate. Under accrual, only types of leave with GAAP-defined liability when earned may be accrued; allowable leave costs are lesser of amount accrued or funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of fringe benefits to cost objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may assign fringe benefits to cost objectives by identifying specific benefits to employees or by allocating them based on entity-wide salaries and wages; when allocation method is used, separate allocations must be made to selective groupings unless differences are insignificant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation must be consistent with the pattern of benefits attributable to employees whose salaries are chargeable to awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance costs and self-insurance reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions for a reserve under a self-insurance program for unemployment or workers' compensation are allowable to the extent they represent reasonable estimates of liabilities and would have been allowable had insurance been purchased; provisions not payable for more than one year must not exceed present value of the liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance costs on lives of trustees/officers are allowable only to extent representing additional compensation; cost of such insurance is unallowable when recipient is named beneficiary. Actual claims paid for workers' comp, unemployment, severance, and similar benefits are allowable in year paid if consistent costing policy is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automobile personal use
rubrics_metrics.description: That portion of automobile costs that relates to personal use by employees (including transportation to/from work) is unallowable as a fringe benefit or indirect cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of whether the cost is reported as taxable income to employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension plan costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Pension plan costs incurred in accordance with established written policies are allowable provided policies are reasonable, allocation methods non-discriminatory, costs assigned in accordance with GAAP (except for State/local governments), and costs for a fiscal year are funded for all participants within six months after the end of that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increases to normal and past service pension costs caused by delays in funding beyond 30 calendar days after each quarter are unallowable. Pension plan costs may be computed using pay-as-you-go or actuarial methods recognized by GAAP; pay-as-you-go allowable costs limited to actual payments to retirees; actuarial costs allowable if funded within six months (or later period agreed by cognizant agency) or allowable in year funded if funded later. Premiums for ERISA termination insurance are allowable; late payment charges, excise taxes on funding deficiencies, and penalties under ERISA are unallowable.
